Synopsis:
    Despite fears of a Japanese sovereign debt crisis driven by PM Takaichi's expansionary fiscal stance and near-200% debt-to-GDP ratio, foreign investors are actively buying Japanese bonds rather than fleeing. A currency hedge arbitrage (rolling 3-month FX forwards) allows western investors to earn a yield pickup of up to 1pp over their domestic government bonds. Japanese domestic institutions (notably GPIF) are not repatriating foreign assets at scale. The BOJ is signalling near-term tightening. The yen remains structurally weak. The overall picture is of contained sovereign risk in Japan, with international capital flows broadly stable.
